findings.note: The hint splices {out} unquoted into a minisign command (src/baseline.rs ~1609); it only misleads for paths with spaces, and the path is printed anyway.
True that --out does not create parent dirs and init does not make baselines/, but the replaced '> baselines/release.json' redirect failed the same way, so the change does not make it worse.
True edge case: the staging name is '.' + name + ~40 chars, so a name near NAME_MAX gets ENAMETOOLONG; this is negligible in practice.
The FAIL (tampered log) refusal returns before the write exactly like the exit-3 refusal that is tested; a thin coverage gap.

The pub fn run rustdoc (src/baseline.rs ~1438) still shows usage without --out and says no --verify 'prints the canonical manifest to stdout', which --out makes false; the commit that changed the behaviour left it stale.

Correct that a direct fs::write after success would pass every test in tests/baseline_out.rs (the rename-fails case also fails with EISDIR); the rename mechanism is not pinned, but the observable refusal guarantee is.
The parent directory is not fsynced after rename; this is a crash-durability nicety for a CLI that writes a file a human then signs.
